# Work Command

> Enter a feature's working context and stay anchored to it. Once active, plain requests
> like "melhora o tratamento de erro" are understood against this feature — no need to
> re-specify which feature or re-explain its design. Closes the post-build gap where every
> tweak forced you to restate context.

## Usage

```bash
/work <FEATURE>      # Enter a feature — loads its context and marks it active
/work                # Resume the currently active feature (reads .active)
/work --status       # Render an HTML "Mission Control" dashboard of the active feature and open it
/work --done         # Clear the active feature (also done automatically by /ship)
```

## Examples

```bash
/work USER_AUTH                  # Anchor the session to USER_AUTH
/work                            # "...where was I?" — resume the active feature
/work --status                   # What's active and what's pending
```

---

## Overview

`/work` is a **cross-phase anchor**, not a new phase. It complements the workflow:

```text
Phase 0: /brainstorm → BRAINSTORM_{FEATURE}.md
Phase 1: /define     → DEFINE_{FEATURE}.md
Phase 2: /design     → DESIGN_{FEATURE}.md
Phase 3: /build      → Code + BUILD_REPORT_{FEATURE}.md + BLACKBOARD_{FEATURE}.md
         /work       → Stay on this feature; route tweaks automatically (THIS COMMAND)
Phase 4: /ship       → archive/{FEATURE}/ (clears .active)
```

The active feature is recorded in `.claude/sdd/.active`, a small pointer file:

```yaml
feature: USER_AUTH
phase: build
updated: 2026-06-21
```

---

## Process

### Step 1: Resolve the Feature

| Invocation | Resolution |
|------------|------------|
| `/work <FEATURE>` | Use the named feature |
| `/work` (no arg) | Read `feature:` from `.claude/sdd/.active` |
| Neither resolves | Auto-detect the most recently modified `DESIGN_*.md` / `BLACKBOARD_*.md` and confirm with the user |

### Step 2: Load Feature Context

Read only what exists, in this order (later phases override earlier for "current truth"):

```markdown
read_file(.claude/sdd/features/DEFINE_{FEATURE}.md)        → acceptance criteria, scope
read_file(.claude/sdd/features/DESIGN_{FEATURE}.md)        → file manifest, decisions
read_file(.claude/sdd/features/BLACKBOARD_{FEATURE}.md)    → live state, interfaces, open items
read_file(.claude/sdd/reports/BUILD_REPORT_{FEATURE}.md)   → what was built and verified
```

Present a compact orientation (do NOT dump full files):

```text
▶ Active feature: {FEATURE}  (phase: {phase})
  Goal      : {one line from DEFINE problem statement}
  Built     : {N files, tests status from BUILD_REPORT}
  Open items: {count of 🔴 blockers + open Melhorias from BLACKBOARD}
  Last change: {most recent Melhorias / Continuation entry}
```

### Step 3: Write the Pointer

```bash
mkdir -p .claude/sdd/
cat > .claude/sdd/.active <<EOF
feature: {FEATURE}
phase: {detected phase}
updated: $(date +%Y-%m-%d)
EOF
```

### Step 4: Route Subsequent Requests (the anchor at work)

While a feature is active, interpret plain requests against it. Classify and route —
do NOT ask the user to restate the feature:

| Request kind | Route to | Example |
|--------------|----------|---------|
| Fix / complete / improve **code** | `/continuar` behavior (gap fix on this feature) | "melhora o tratamento de erro", "faltou o retry" |
| Change a **requirement or design** | `/iterate` behavior on DEFINE/DESIGN | "agora precisa suportar CSV também" |
| Question about the feature | Answer from loaded context | "como ficou o schema?" |

**Every routed change is logged to the blackboard** under "Melhorias / Iterações" so the
feature keeps a running history (this is the feature's working memory):

```markdown
| M-001 | {data} | {pedido do usuário} | código/design | @{agente} | ✅ |
```

### Status Dashboard (`--status`)

`/work --status` renders a self-contained **HTML "Mission Control"** of the active feature
from the files already on disk (`.active`, `BLACKBOARD`, `BUILD_REPORT`) — a progress strip
(completos / em andamento / pendentes / bloqueados / melhorias) plus the rendered blackboard
and build report. No server, no tokens spent rendering — a deterministic script does it.

```bash
# Resolves the feature from .active (or pass one explicitly), writes the HTML, prints its path
DASH=$(python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-.}/scripts/status-dashboard.py" 2>/dev/null)
[ -n "$DASH" ] && open "$DASH" 2>/dev/null || echo "Dashboard: $DASH"
```

Output: `.claude/sdd/.status/dashboard.html`. It is a static snapshot — re-run `/work --status`
to refresh. This is AgentSpec's answer to "see what's happening" without a daemon or web app:
the blackboard and build report ARE the live state; this just renders them.

### Step 5: Stay Anchored

The feature stays active across turns until:

- the user runs `/work <OTHER>` (switch),
- the user runs `/work --done`, or
- `/ship` archives the feature (clears `.active` automatically).

---

## Why This Closes the Gap

Without `/work`, each post-build "improve X" forces you to re-name the feature and the model
to re-load its context — burning tokens and losing nuance. With `/work`:

- the feature is named **once**; the pointer remembers it,
- the model reads DESIGN + BLACKBOARD instead of asking you to re-explain,
- improvements accumulate on the blackboard, not in scattered chat history,
- when you return later, `/work` (no arg) restores exactly where you were.

It is the orchestrator-level companion to the blackboard: the blackboard anchors the
**specialists** during a build; `/work` anchors **you** across the whole feature.

---

## Quality Gate

```text
[ ] Feature resolved (named, from .active, or confirmed auto-detect)
[ ] Existing artifacts loaded (compact orientation shown, not full dumps)
[ ] .claude/sdd/.active written with feature + phase + date
[ ] Subsequent change requests routed (code → continuar, docs → iterate)
[ ] Each change logged to BLACKBOARD "Melhorias / Iterações"
```
